answer: Sybil resistance can be grown, not bought: each seat keeps a juniper sawdust bed inoculated with a registered fungal strain, kept beside a working forge whose waste heat makes bed temperature swing with real shifts. Every epoch the operator submits a 24-hour trace of the mycelium's spontaneous electrical pulse train. Spikes come from living metabolism tied to that heat rhythm, so two seats sharing one bed emit identical trains and are flagged as one operator. Faking a farm needs one bed, one recorder and one running forge per identity, plus months of cultivation, for one seat's payout.
